beats.summary: Michael tries to decide what to write in wet cement outside, seeking ideas from coworkers.

evidence.snippet: Michael: Everybody! Everybody! Listen up, I need your ideas, now! Ideas please, right now! Go! Go! Come on!
Michael: Wet cement, outside. It's drying fast, come on. This is a lifelong dream. What do I write? What do I write?

beats.summary: Michael puts petroleum jelly on his face and presses it into the cement to leave an imprint.

evidence.snippet: Michael (with petroleum jelly on his face): Hurry, please.
Michael sticks his face in the cement

beats.summary: Michael explains the significance of the cement imprint as a legacy for his descendants.

evidence.snippet: Michael: Today is a very special day for me. And it's really not about me, it's about my grandkids, it's about my great grandkids…

beats.summary: Jim proposes to Pam during a meeting but only asks her to get him coffee.

evidence.snippet: Jim: Well, it's too late, because I'm proposing… that you get me a cup of coffee, which would energize me greatly, and make me the happiest man in the world.
Pam: If you propose to me during a Michael meeting, I will say no.

beats.summary: Stanley openly defies Michael during a brainstorming session by saying 'DID I STUTTER?'

evidence.snippet: Michael: We're havin a little brainstorm session…

beats.summary: Michael refuses to take Toby's advice to address Stanley's insubordination seriously, claiming it was a joke between friends.

evidence.snippet: Toby: Uh, I really think that you need to address what happened with Stanley this morning…
Michael: We were joshin around, the two of us, and he said "did I stutter," and I said "wha-wha-wha-wha-what, dawg?" It was joking, Toby, alright?
